factor_audit.positive_evidence: Useful disclosure and completed mandatory audit rotation; published debt reduction supports some discipline.
factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Large scope-changing buyout, parent recourse, promoter pledge, nested minority interests and reliability questions prevent an aligned-stewardship premium.

factor_audit.positive_evidence: Real-estate sourcing networks, fund licences and 5–7 year closed-end mandates make relationships useful and fees somewhat durable.
factor_audit.adverse_evidence: No independently verified persistent fee premium or superior full-cycle realized fund returns; advisers and managers compete for institutional capital.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: 4 understates established mandates; 6 requires repeatable exits and documented customer retention/fee pricing power.

factor_audit.positive_evidence: Five-year retained-fee CAGR is the declared economic basis; numerical starting score 9 because CAGR≥30%. Fees exclude EPC and own-investment gains.
factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Mix/geography expansion and small-base dynamics limit organic comparability; a single soft Q1 is insufficient for a trajectory penalty. Confidence ceiling caps 9 to 8, with net trajectory adjustment 0.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: 7 would add an unsupported discretionary penalty after scope correction; 9 needs high-confidence comparable organic fee cohorts and sustained current progression.

factor_audit.positive_evidence: Institutional/private real estate credit, new domestic and UAE funds and construction backlog create multiple plausible avenues.
factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Real estate/funding cycles, exits, geopolitical delays and construction collection risk constrain accessible demand; tokenization and SMREIT remain optional.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: 5 understates established funds and existing operating access; 7 needs evidence of funded executable runway rather than launches alone.

factor_audit.positive_evidence: Fee business can be capital-light and AUM not owned capital; portfolio principal and acquisition leverage are explicitly separated.
factor_audit.adverse_evidence: No reliable incremental after-tax fee profit versus capitalized origination/launch spend, attributable own-investment loss-adjusted return and paid/retained acquisition capital bridge. Group ROCE would mix incompatible engines and ownership.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: NS is not an assumed 5; score requires comparable risk-adjusted realized return and attributable reinvestment schedule. Industrial incremental NOPAT/IC deliberately not imposed.

factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Investment return classification, acquired EPC working capital and capitalized fundraising costs prevent isolating multi-year operating fee collection/carry realization. Negative group CFO is material but not a sector-correct standalone CASH 3 rule.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: NS is not benign: aged assets and nonaccrual require closure. Persistent-poor-realization GQS ceiling evaluated; not established on comparable fee-cash basis, so no automatic cap. If evidenced CASH≤3, cap GQS 5 even if point stays NS.

factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Restricted cash, material bank-return differences/current drawing power, acquisition guarantees and legal cash fungibility block a verified current funding bridge. Not simply lack of daily bank statements.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: Neither a neutral 5 nor a distress score is justified. Need current cash/debt/facility bridge, accepted collateral returns and dated debt maturities/recourse.

factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Full-cycle exits sparse, construction integration remains recent and Q1 core income softened. Headline core profit includes treasury gains.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: 4 overstates proven repeated failure; 6 requires delivery of cash realizations, promised fund exits and stable construction collections.

factor_audit.adverse_evidence: ₹31.3583 investment gains plus tax-refund interest/FX/tax credits and acquired EPC profit materially influence headline results. No defensible precise recurring owner EPS; Q1 parent PAT fell 30.2%.
factor_audit.why_not_higher_or_lower: 3 would imply profit growth is mainly unsupported; 5 needs recurring fee-profit and per-share progression after removing volatile/nonoperating effects.

factor_audit.adverse_evidence: Current funding unverified; every non-rescue case breaches modeled cash floor, so ordinary and conditional non-rescue IRRs are NS.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. This is not a clean, capital-light asset-manager compounding case at the consolidated level. Strong fee growth coexists with a newly acquired, leveraged construction business, volatile investment gains, significant minority interests and material collateral-return reconciliation differences. Audited FY2026 owner PAT is ₹70.3479 crore, not the group ₹83.0834 crore. Neither figure is a defensible recurring fee-profit base. BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS remain NS rather than neutral scores; there is no ordinary target price or return claim. The main impediments are G2 financial reliability and G3 current funding, not a conclusion of fraud or historical default. Conditional research only; not an evidence-backed compounder candidate.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Identity: Nisus Finance Services Co Limited, CIN L65923MH2013PLC247317, BSE SME 544296, symbol NISUS, ISIN INE0DQN01013. Listed 11 December 2024; accounting follows Indian AS, not Ind AS. Analysis cutoff 20 October 2026; price reference 19 October 2026, secondary dated close ₹167.65. Retrieved 22 October, but post-cutoff economic data are excluded. The five-year hurdle runs 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 using actual 1826 days/365.25, nominal 15% pre-investor-tax, with 12/18% sensitivities and an illustrative ₹500,000 position. Annual accounts are primary audited/restated sources; June 2026 results are limited-reviewed, management AUM is separately labeled. G1 and G4 Conditional, G2 and G3 Hold—unresolved. Original full reports were inspected, including main opinions and available annexures; source-safe extracts permit model reproduction, not re-authentication of originals.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical primitives: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH NS, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 4, R NS, D NS, P NS, L NS. Every known integer is evidence-anchored below. BQS known contribution 3.96 with 70% weight coverage and mathematically possible 4.26–6.96; GQS known 5.00 with 75% coverage and 5.25–7.50. IAS has no point coverage; its primitive 1–10 bound is not a probable interval. A tighter bound uses the unresolved BQS envelope, not a substituted midpoint. No missing factor receives 5 and no weights are renormalized. Persistent poor cash realization is explicitly evaluated: the mixed proprietary-investment/manager/EPC cash flows do not establish comparable fee realization, so CASH stays NS and a mechanical GQS ceiling is not applied. If persistent CASH≤3 or CAP≤3 becomes evidenced, GQS ceiling 5 must apply, including its diagnostic upper bound when the point remains NS. No ranking eligibility while material gates and factors remain unresolved. One-point sensitivity for the two most uncertain scored judgments is explicit: GOV 5 to 4 or 6, or MOAT 5 to 4 or 6, independently shifts the BQS known contribution and both raw bounds by minus or plus 0.20. The corresponding BQS ranges are 4.06–6.76 and 4.46–7.16; moving both down/up shifts them by 0.40. GQS is unchanged, IAS stays NS and its nested bounds move by 0.05 per individual change. All nine joint combinations are retained below, with no missing-factor imputation or ranking eligibility. GOV <=3 on sufficient adverse evidence or G1 failure would separately activate the governance override, cap final BQS/IAS at 3 and require Avoid — governance; this is not established here.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Three engines must be separated. First, domestic and international real-estate fund management/advice earns management fees and transaction/advisory income from third-party capital. Second, own NCD/AIF/NBFC exposure earns interest and investment gains while bearing principal/default risk. Third, NCCCL executes construction contracts, holds inventory, receivables and bank guarantees, and carries working-capital debt. The latter enters audited consolidation from 21 August 2025: FY26 included total income ₹433.8995 crore and PAT ₹15.3345 crore. Control is not full economics: parent owns 73.83% of Projects LLP, which holds 54.03% of NCCCL at year-end, implying 39.890349% proportional economic participation; exact distribution rights remain a sensitivity. Actual historical owner PAT uses audited attribution, not those end-year percentages. Managed AUM ₹2631 crore is client capital, not issuer NAV, freely usable cash or acquisition funding.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The useful advantages are local sourcing, real-estate underwriting relationships, fund-management infrastructure and closed-end 5–7 year mandates. These can stabilize contractual management fees and make repeat fundraising easier, but a licence or brand alone is not an economic moat. Advisory income ₹75.3704 crore materially exceeds ₹20.2790 crore management fees in FY26, so revenues are not predominantly fixed annuities. CARE identifies limited realized full-cycle exits and concentrated real-estate exposure. Only one of three active funds exceeded its hurdle at that review, partly using unrealized gains; last realized carry was from REAP 2020. Independent persistent fee premium, loss-adjusted fund performance, client retention and actual carry cash are not sufficiently evidenced for MOAT 7+. Construction qualification and order access offer operating relevance but do not eliminate tender competition, claims or collection risk.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The chosen comparable economic cross-check is retained advisory plus management fees, not consolidated total revenue or AUM. The six annual fee observations are ₹4.0308/5.5677/6.1420/37.9782/56.9597/95.6494 crore for FY21–FY26. Five-year retained-fee CAGR is 88.39% and three-year CAGR 149.72%; both are calculated from the complete embedded rows; acquisition construction and own investment sale gains are excluded. The five-year result starts REV 9 under the framework’s ≥30% schedule; Medium confidence in the expanding fund/geography mix caps the final factor at 8, with trajectory adjustment 0. No additional small-base penalty is stacked onto scope correction. FY26 group operating revenue ₹561.0050 versus ₹64.7321 is mostly an acquired-perimeter change, not organic growth. AUM rose 1572 to 2631, which corroborates scale but is not recognized fee revenue. Q1 FY27 management core total income ₹27.6 versus ₹28.7237 prior is approximately −3.9%; a single soft quarter does not itself justify the sustained-trajectory penalty. TTM group revenue ₹717.5932 and owner PAT ₹65.4720 are explicitly mixed-perimeter, not clean organic run rates.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The accessible runway is additional fee-paying real-estate mandates, repeat investors and domestic/UAE deployment. Future carry, SMREITs and the $500 million tokenization MoU are options, not funded recurring income. Additional AUM has a different capital burden from owned investments or construction revenue. We therefore do not score CAP from industrial group incremental NOPAT/invested capital: cash launch/distribution spend is capitalized, proprietary returns include credit losses/gains, and acquisition capital plus NCI changed sharply. FY26 unamortized launch-type balances ₹41.4083 crore versus ₹21.7805 earlier and amortization ₹13.1028 demonstrate that fundraising is not free. Our fee model charges recurring distribution cash even after the IPO budget expires, separately models issuer-owned investment principal and credit loss, and gives EPC its own working capital/capex/interest. Sponsor commitment ₹2.24 is included once. Sustainable attributable fee return on reinvestment, realized own-portfolio returns and acquisition after-financing yield remain open.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The record contains actual fundraising and substantial fee growth, completion of NCCCL control acquisition, reduction of acquisition borrowings ₹110 to ₹38 crore, and actual July 31 repayment of Fincorp’s remaining ₹5.5 crore. These are positives rather than ignored counterevidence. The buyout also changes listed-shareholder risk: acquisition lenders have parent corporate guarantee/current-asset charge, promoter personal guarantee and listed/target-share pledges. Primary ₹70 crore subscribed into NCCCL is group capital, not automatically a seller payment; undisclosed seller consideration is not invented. Ending ownership and nested NCI prevent attributing 100% construction economics to listed holders. June 2026 promoter holding 73.98%, total pledged 23.70% of issuer shares, with Fincorp pledge release still in process in that filing. MD remuneration ₹2.4318 versus ₹1.0397 FY25 is 3.46% of owner PAT; spouse remuneration ₹0.2463, MD loan interest ₹0.8492 and profit share ₹4.4404 are separately disclosed, not conflated with salary. No guarantee commission is stated. No ESOP grants by June 2026; trust secondary market purchases do not create issued dilution. Mandatory auditor rotation is not an adverse resignation. CARE’s narrower exclusion of NCCCL operating obligations is distinguished from the parent’s explicit acquisition-debt guarantee. GOV 5/EXEC 5 reflect real progress with material unresolved allocation/integration concerns, not an allegation of abuse.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: G2 is constrained by quantified bank-return differences, not just ratios. June 2025 reported debtors and stock exceeded books by ₹54.7870/32.5997 crore; March 2026 books exceeded returns by ₹27.9563/33.0211. All eight quarterly/category rows and management’s early unaudited-submission/closing-adjustment/SAP migration explanation are retained. A clean audit, CARO summary, IFC and audit-trail opinion coexist with these differences; none authenticates present drawing power. FY26 free cash is ₹7.6128 of ₹25.2207 reported current cash, with ₹17.6079 liens and further ₹14.4517 long restricted FD/₹2.7788 restricted MF. Old tax provision ₹13.9177, statutory ₹6.0846, salaries ₹22.8791, interest ₹0.3191, other expenses ₹4.8928 and MSME interest ₹1.9171 plus current benefits ₹3.4398 are modeled as one-time cash liabilities outside assumed operating capital; ₹40.8874 government assets are not assumed tax offsets. Unpaid MSME interest is credit quality counterevidence, not bank default. CFO ₹−20.1895 precedes finance outflow ₹25.6287 and cash capex ₹14.6575. Fees versus proprietary investment flows cannot be cleanly separated, so CFO/PAT is diagnostic, not a lender/asset manager scoring formula. Nonaccrued interest ₹2.8805 and past-due NCD notes matter; do not label the entire ₹61.6580 NCD book overdue. Receivables include ₹96.2087 unbilled, ₹26.8288 good balances over one year and ₹14.8680 provision. Completed properties ₹49.3573 received against dues are noncash recovery, excluded from our terminal value with zero additional collection assumption. This is conservative potential upside, not worthless collateral. FY25 FD-interest revenue/CFO regrouping, balance netting and D&A presentation are reconciled rather than called fraud. Published FY25 EPS uses group PAT; corrected attributable EPS is separately derived. Investment gain ₹31.3583, refund interest ₹6.9394, FX ₹3.6102 and tax credits preclude treating management core PAT ₹67.7489 as recurring owner fee profit.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Use a hybrid sum-of-parts, not consolidated industrial EV/EBITDA or an indiscriminate headline P/E. The fee franchise is valued on modeled unlevered after-tax attributable fee operating earnings (an EV/NOPAT-style multiple, not P/E); owned investment capital on net book× recovery, with no second capitalization of its yield; construction on post-interest equity earnings× effective ownership. Acquisition/core debt and unidentified ₹4.4396 share application claim are deducted, EPC debt not deducted twice, signed cash surplus after an operating reserve included once. No extra value for operating property or managed AUM. Annual and interval rows include recurring launch costs, collection investment, owned principal/credit loss, EPC capex, scheduled debt, restricted cash exclusion and precise horizon. Bear/base/bull non-rescue cases all breach conservative pre-receipt cash floors before entry. These are stress assumptions, not proof of an actual unpaid obligation. Consequently ordinary IRRs/entry prices and non-rescue conditional IRRs are NS. Separately labeled counterfactual pre-March whole-share rescue cases pre-fund the largest trough at ₹160 with 2% fees, assume priority parent funding repayment capped by actual surplus cash (no negative minority cash claim), reconcile net/gross and dilution and provide diagnostic returns/hurdle prices only. Audited authorized 25,000,000 shares leave only 1,121,900 headroom; every modeled rescue requires authorized-capital increase and shareholder/regulatory approvals. They are not announced funding or buy recommendations. Reverse ordinary growth is NS; rescue reverse solver reports only finite funded crossings/residuals. Two-way growth× multiple, collections× EPC capex, reserve× asset recovery and cash attribution× EPC ownership tests are fully embedded.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Permanent loss can arise without revenue collapse: weak fund exits lower advisory/carry cash, credit recovery delays lock up owned principal, and construction customer delays absorb inventory/receivables while bank drawing power is questioned. Parent recourse links the former platform to leveraged acquisition obligations; forced sales/pledge realization or dilutive refinancing can shift value away from current holders. Large nominal facilities are not available cash: ₹430 crore total less ₹169.0279 fund draw and ₹187.0169 BG leaves an arithmetic ₹73.9552, before eligibility/margins and with no verified bank-accepted DP. Acuité 3 February 2026 independently rates NCCCL BBB+ Stable/A2, calls liquidity adequate and projects ₹30–45 crore NCA versus ₹5–9 crore repayments. This is real positive counterevidence, not a whole-group funding guarantee. Its 86.08% funded utilization, ₹92.39 crore retention and 336 day GCA also show cash intensity. Rated ₹500 crore includes ₹50.70 proposed facilities, not sanctioned spendable cash; dated 60.83% ownership differs from later audited 54.03%. Existing properties/NCD collateral and actual debt paydown are counterevidence to a zero-recovery assumption, but not timely liquidity. The bear model charges credit loss, lower fee growth/margins and slower collections; rescue dilution is explicit. G3 Hold is driven by these concrete constraints, not mere lack of private daily bank data. No historical default or insolvency claim is made from modeled negative cash.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At ₹167.65, undiluted 5×/10× prices are ₹838.25/₹1676.50, requiring about 38%/58% annual price appreciation over the exact five-year horizon. These are arithmetic hurdles, not return forecasts. The embedded tests hold non-fee terminal parts and a 12× fee multiple at base assumptions, then solve the unlevered fee NOPAT and revenue needed to reach those equity values; no managed AUM is added to market value. The exercise also flags that any rescue/share issuance raises the required aggregate equity beyond the undiluted illustration. Exceptional repeated fundraising, pricing, profitable deployment, actual fee/carry collection and a durable funding arrangement would all need to coexist. AUM growth alone or cheap headline P/E cannot establish this. Current evidence and unresolved financial gates do not support an evidence-backed 5×/10× thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Before investable reconsideration: 1) obtain bank-accepted corrections for all quarterly collateral returns and a currently eligible drawing power bridge; 2) reconcile post-July redemption cash, debt maturity/renewals, collateral liens and parent/subsidiary cash access; 3) separate fee/advisory income, carry, treasury gains, related-party balances and cash collections; 4) reconcile nested NCI and acquisition cash/capital waterfall; 5) track overdue NCD recoveries and noncash property sale proceeds without double counting; 6) test fee-profit after recurring launch/distribution cash; 7) authenticate BSE 20/60-session turnover, zero/no-row classifications, 400 share lot, spreads and restrictions. Earnings watch: two comparable halves of fee progress and cash realization, construction debtor aging/guarantees and exits supporting carried interest. Escalate on auditor qualification, unexplained collateral differences, actual default/covenant breach, compulsory collateral sale or unfair related-party allocation. Improve the assessment only on documented closure, not another growth presentation.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification: Hold — unresolved, with separate insufficient-evidence factors. Do not rank BQS/GQS/IAS or call this an attractive compounder using partially computed scores. The ₹500,000 reference position can fit 7 whole lots/2800 shares for ₹469,420; 8 lots/3200 shares cost ₹536,480, but neither says the trade can execute. No prescribed allocation, ordinary entry price or investment return is supported. Keep a research watchlist conditional on G2 / G3 closure and actual BSE liquidity evidence; reconsider valuation only after recurring attributable fee economics and current funding are independently reconciled. Positive evidence of real fee scale, debt paydown and asset collateral remains visible so future updating can improve rather than merely repeat a negative narrative.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: All key claims link to identified issuer annual reports, results/limited review, acquisition notices, earnings calls, CARE rationale or official master. Dated secondary price is distinctly labeled; inaccessible official BSE history is disclosed rather than synthesized. Full raw documents are not redistributed; safe extracts retain locators, URLs and retrieved file hashes. The reproducible model explicitly marks assumed fee profit margin, receivable timing, cash fungibility, ownership attribution, term allocation, funding reserve, credit loss, dilution and terminal multiples. Missing exact seller consideration, fee profit/cash collections, ultimate legal distribution rights, current bank DP/cash, overdue NCD principal and actual trading liquidity stay ND/NS. Historical ordinary cash classification changes do not automatically indicate misconduct. Source-safe reproduction proves arithmetic/data handling only, not correctness of an unobserved transaction or current cash balance. Primary economic facts cutoff 20 October 2026; no 21 October price or later operating results are smuggled in.

summary: Hold — unresolved. This is not a clean, capital-light asset-manager compounding case at the consolidated level. Strong fee growth coexists with a newly acquired, leveraged construction business, volatile investment gains, significant minority interests and material collateral-return reconciliation differences. Audited FY2026 owner PAT is ₹70.3479 crore, not the group ₹83.0834 crore. Neither figure is a defensible recurring fee-profit base. BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS remain NS rather than neutral scores; there is no ordinary target price or return claim. The main impediments are G2 financial reliability and G3 current funding, not a conclusion of fraud or historical default. Conditional research only; not an evidence-backed compounder candidate.
